title: Comparative efficacy of modern antithrombotic regimens for saphenous vein graft patency after coronary artery bypass grafting: A systematic review and network meta-analysis
content:
by Ayesha Irshad Ansari, Muhammad Faraz Tariq, Muhammad Usman Khan

Background

Saphenous vein graft (SVG) occlusion remains common after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) despite aspirin. We compared contemporary postoperative antithrombotic regimens for preserving SVG patency.

Methods

We conducted a systematic review and frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. MEDLINE, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 2026. The primary outcome was graft-level SVG occlusion. Aspirin was the reference treatment. Inconsistency was assessed using design-by-treatment interaction and node-splitting. Because multiple SVGs could arise from the same patient, we added a post-hoc variance-inflation sensitivity analysis using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) of 0.15, 0.20, and 0.25.

Results

Fifteen trials met review criteria; 10 contributed to the primary network (6,934 SVGs, 22 treatment arms, 7 nodes). Aspirin plus ticagrelor reduced SVG occlusion versus aspirin alone (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.34–0.80; p = 0.003). Aspirin plus clopidogrel showed a non-significant possible benefit (OR 0.62, 95% CI 0.38–1.04; p = 0.070). Other regimens were not significantly different from aspirin. Aspirin plus ticagrelor ranked highest (P-score 0.88). Heterogeneity was moderate (I² = 52.6%). The aspirin plus ticagrelor finding remained significant after clustering variance inflation across ICCs 0.15–0.25 (adjusted OR approximately 0.53; all p ≤ 0.006).

Conclusions

Aspirin plus ticagrelor was associated with lower graft-level SVG occlusion, but SVG patency is a surrogate outcome. Randomized evidence has not established corresponding reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events or mortality, while intensified dual antiplatelet therapy may increase bleeding. Treatment should therefore be individualized.

Registration

This review was not prospectively registered. An a posteriori protocol and data repository was archived on OSF after screening and analysis had commenced: https://osf.io/qfwc9/.
